transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
I've just not been sleeping well at all, that's the main thing. I was hoping the doctor could give me something to help me sleep.
Can you tell me when you first started having trouble sleeping and how it came about, and also whether you have any allergies or bad reactions to medicines?
The sleep trouble came on a while back, I'm not sure exactly when. And no, I've never had any bad reactions to medicines that I know of.
How much is your trouble sleeping affecting your daily life?
It's been getting me down, honestly. I'm too tired to get down to my allotment these days, and I find myself dozing off in the chair in the afternoon.
What medicines are you taking at the moment?
Just some tablets for my blood pressure and one for my waterworks, that sort of thing. Nothing unusual, I don't think.
Have you ever had an operation or been in hospital?
No, I've never had an operation or been in hospital for anything. Just the usual check-ups for my blood pressure.
Besides feeling tired and dozing off in the afternoon, have you noticed anything else going on with your health around the time your sleep is troubling you?
Well, my mood's been a bit low at times, if I'm honest. That's sort of come on since I retired.
Where do you notice the trouble with your sleep most?
It's mostly in the early hours, I'd say. I drop off alright but then I'm awake and can't get back over again.
Have you noticed anything that seems to make it harder to get back to sleep when you wake in the early hours?
I think if I've had a late night watching the telly it's worse. On days when I've been out for a good long walk it's better, I sleep a bit more soundly.
When you're having trouble with your sleep, where do you notice it most — is it in your head, in your body, or does it spread to other places, or you're not sure?
I'm not sure really — it's not in any particular place. It's just that my head won't switch off and I'm lying there wide awake.
Besides your usual blood pressure check-ups, is there anything else from your past health — like other health problems or illnesses — you'd like to add?
Yes, I've got high blood pressure, and I've got a bit of trouble with an enlarged prostate as well. That's what the waterworks tablet is for.
When you're lying awake in the night like that, what does it feel like for you?
It's frustrating more than anything — I'm tired but my mind is just going, and I can't seem to drop off again. Some nights I end up getting barely a few hours.
Along with the sleep trouble, and apart from your mood being a bit low, is there anything else you'd like to add?
No, I don't think I snore — the wife never mentioned it, and I've never nodded off at the wheel. Although I have been trying some tablets from the pharmacy to help me sleep.
Did your sleep trouble start suddenly, come on gradually, or are you not sure?
It came on gradually, I'd say. It was around the time I retired, about three months ago, looking back.
Besides your blood pressure and the prostate problem you mentioned, is there anything else about your past health you’d like to add?
No, that's about the lot as far as my health goes. Just the blood pressure and the prostate, nothing else I can think of.
Have you noticed any other changes or symptoms since your sleep trouble started?
Not really, other than being worn out all the time. I do keep taking those pharmacy sleeping tablets most nights, though they don't seem to be helping much.
Other than the sleeping tablets you mentioned, are you taking any other medicines regularly, or have you started or changed any recently, or are you not sure?

Well, there's the one for my blood pressure, losartan, 50 milligrams once a day. And the waterworks one, tamsulosin, 400 micrograms at night. Then the pharmacy sleeping tablets, most nights for the last few weeks.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
